newsitem.title: USA: No talks planned in IBP Illinois beef plant strike.
newsitem.headline: No talks planned in IBP Illinois beef plant strike.

text.p: No negotiations were scheduled for this week between IBP Inc and striking meat cutters at the company's Joslin, Ill., cattle slaughter and beef processing plant, company and union spokesmen said.
About 1,800 meat cutters, members of United Food and Commercial Workers Local 1540, struck Wednesday after they rejected the company's latest contract offer.
Industry sources estimate the plant can slaughter 2,000 to 3,000 cattle per day.
"We have shifted production to other plants," said IBP spokesman Gary Mickelson. "We have more than enough capacity at other plants."
Both sides said they have been in contact with the federal mediator since the strike began and are willing to resume talks, but no negotiations have been scheduled.
Bob Hooker, Local 1540 secretary-treasurer, said the meat cutters oppose the company's plan to scale back insurance coverage and profit sharing.
